name: Saburô Uchiyama
note: A Japanese analytic number theorist whose work covered the distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions and integers representable as sums of two squares, including a short-interval conjecture that bears his name. He is the doctoral advisor of Koichi Kawada, which places him directly beside the Top 100 in the genealogy graph.

name: Anatoly Alekseevich Karatsuba
note: A foundational Russian number theorist known for his work on exponential sums and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. The fast Karatsuba multiplication algorithm also bears his name.

name: Olli Järviniemi
note: A young Finnish number theorist with a recent PhD. The genealogy graph reaches him through close advisor-student ties to Kaisa Matomaki and Terence Tao.

name: Russell Sherman Lehman
note: An older-generation analytic number theorist who computed early numerical tables. He enters the graph through the mid-twentieth-century Stanford lineage.

name: Robert Tijdeman
note: A Dutch number theorist, long based at Leiden University, known for Diophantine equations and Diophantine approximation. His 1976 theorem showing Catalan's equation has only finitely many solutions was a major step toward the eventual proof of Catalan's conjecture.

name: Chengdong Pan (潘承洞)
note: One of the founders of the Chinese school of Goldbach research and a student of Hua Luogeng. He did major work on the Goldbach problem through the 1960s and 1970s.
